sense: with a past participle: I had seen

evidence: Plin. Ep. 8.20.3: quod nec audieram ante nec vīderam
Liv. 40.21.2: cupīdō eum cēperat in verticem Haemī montis ascendendī
terms.comment: What was already done before a moment in the past. Passives and deponents form it with eram: ventum erat, they had arrived. After postquam and ubi Latin usually keeps the perfect where English has “had”. “If I had …” is the pluperfect subjunctive (see would).

phrases.latin: quod nec audieram ante nec vīderam, audīvī pariter et vīdī
phrases.english: what I had neither heard of nor seen before, I heard about and saw at the same moment

phrases.latin: cupīdō eum cēperat in verticem Haemī montis ascendendī
phrases.english: he had been seized by a longing to climb to the top of Mount Haemus
they had happened to reach the Janiculum
Oh, Demea, I hadn’t seen you.

phrases.latin: tantum quod mihi nōn dīxerat, quid prīdiē cēnāveram
phrases.english: the only thing he hadn’t told me was what I’d had for dinner the day before
